body:
leah: Hi all, quick question about carryover for a contractor who missed the year-end because they were sick and unable to take PTO during the mandatory shutdown.
paul: Do contractors follow the same 5-day carryover cap? I thought contractors had slightly different rules.
peopleops: Short answer: contractors are usually paid out for unused PTO at year-end unless there's an approved exception. We can make exceptions in extenuating circumstances (long-term illness, FMLA-type overlap) but it requires docs + manager note.
leah: The contractor (Tony) had a 3-week hospital stay in Nov and couldn't take any planned PTO; he was officially out on an approved medical absence, but payroll still shows a full payout queued for Jan. Can we hold payout and convert to carryover?
tony: yep that's my situation - medical leave paperwork filed in HR portal, manager approved LOA. I wanted to ask if those days could be marked as carryover so I can schedule them next year instead of a payout.
peopleops: Please file an exception request using the same HR Exception form (https://intranet.redwood/hr/forms/pto-exception) and attach the LOA docs plus a 1-line manager confirmation. We'll route to Payroll and Legal.
paul: Policy excerpt for reference:
```
Contractor PTO & Carryover (excerpt):
- Standard: Contractor unused PTO is paid out at calendar year close.
- Exception: Contractors with documented medical LOA overlapping mandatory shutdown may be eligible for temporary carryover at People Ops discretion.
- Approval: Requires HR + manager signoff; exceptions > 5 days need Finance approval for accounting notes.
```
peopleops: If you submit by Dec 10 we can stop the auto-payout trigger. After payroll cutoff it's much harder to reverse.
payroll-bot: automated reminder: payroll cutoff for year-end payout reversal is 2023-12-12 17:00 PST. Submit exception before cutoff to pause auto-pay.
leah: Thanks, filing now and attaching LOA + manager note. Tony, I'll cc you on the form.
ton y: thanks leah. small Q: if we convert to carryover, will contractor accruals for next year change or is it just a one-time special bucket?
peopleops: It will be a one-time "temporary carryover" bucket for Q1 only; accrual rules for contractors remain unchanged. We'll add a comment in the payroll memo so accounts treat it as non-recurring.
paul: Noted for finance: if approved please mark memo as "contractor medical carryover - nonrecurring" so we don't double-count in budgets.
peopleops: Got it. I'll track the form and confirm once payroll halts the payout. Expect an update in 48-72 hours after submission.
tony: Really appreciate it, thanks everyone.
leah: thanks team :pray:
